companion.raw.what: put bytes of the caller's own choosing on a node's companion port, for when what the firmware makes of a frame is the thing in question

params.name: node
params.what: the connected node; refused when nothing is connected to it

params.name: bytes
params.what: the payload, one number per byte; anything in the array that is not a number is dropped, and an empty or absent array is refused

params.name: at_ms
params.what: an instant of simulated time to run this at instead of now: the call is held and runs when the engine reaches it, so it lands at the same instant on any machine. Refused unless it is after now. Without it, a call made while the clock is playing lands wherever the clock happens to be, and sim.state then says the run cannot be reproduced

companion.raw.answers: `sent_bytes` counts what was framed and written, which is the numbers that survived, not the length of the array as it was passed.

example.what: hand the firmware three bytes and see what it makes of them
